interface.title: Minerva Story (minerva-browser) – multiplexed tissue exhibit viewer
interface.field: Digital pathology / multiplexed tissue imaging (CyCIF immunofluorescence plus H&E), tumour immunology
interface.stage_of_work: Exploring, interpreting and sharing finished whole-slide images; publishing a narrated data story
interface.what_it_is_for: Browsing a full-resolution multiplexed tissue image in a web page: switching and recolouring marker channels, following a collaborator's narrated waypoints, and sharing annotated views as links.

data.note: exhibit.json loads automatically. It is one colorectal tumour section with an H&E image and 18 CyCIF channels (Hoechst, Autofluorescence, CD31, alpha-SMA, CD4, FOXP3, CD8a, E-cadherin, CD68, PD-L1, CD163, Ki67, CD45RO, CD20, CD3e, PD-1, CD45, Pan-CK). It has six preset channel groups (H&E, Autofluorescence, Immune 1/2/3, Overview) and a three-waypoint story (Introduction, Multimodal Lensing, Multimodal). It has no cell-segmentation masks or data overlays: the mask parameter in the URL stays m=-1 throughout.

features.name: Channel legend with per-channel show/hide, recolour and add
features.general: Pick a preset set of image layers, then hide individual layers, change their colours, or add more layers to make a custom set
features.specific: Choose a channel group, press the gear to enter edit mode, toggle eye icons, recolour with the eyedropper palette and Update, add channels with ⊕ (which creates a new group such as 'Autofluorescence (1)'), and close with ⊗
steps: click eye icon to hide/show a channel
click eyedropper, choose a colour, press Update
press ⊕ and pick a channel to add
serves_tasks: Switch between preset combinations of markers
Turn individual layers on and off to compare markers
Change the display colour of a layer
Build a custom combination by adding another layer

features.name: Narrated waypoint story panel
features.general: A guided tour where each numbered stop sets the view and the layers and shows explanatory text, with next/previous, a contents list and in-text jump links
features.specific: Step through waypoints 1/3 to 3/3 with ← / →, or open the Table of Contents (on the Introduction stop) to jump to a waypoint. Each waypoint applies its channel group, viewport and (for waypoint 2) a lens. In this exhibit the inline link (#s=1w=0) is malformed and lands on 3/3 instead of the lens stop
steps: open the Table of Contents icon
click a waypoint title or an inline link
serves_tasks: Step forward and back through narrated stops
Jump straight to a stop from a contents list or an in-text link

features.name: Movable, resizable comparison lens
features.general: A circular magnifier that shows a second image type (here brightfield) inside a draggable, resizable circle over the main image, so two images of the same spot can be compared
features.specific: On the Multimodal Lensing waypoint, an H&E lens floats over the CyCIF Overview group. Drag it to move, drag the ↔ handle to resize, and toggle base-layer channels while the lens keeps showing H&E
steps: drag the lens body to a region
hide or show base-layer channels while the lens stays
serves_tasks: Compare two imaging types at the same spot with a movable lens

features.name: Arrow annotation to shareable-link dialog
features.general: Drop a pointer on an image, attach a short note, and get a URL that reopens the view, pointer and note for a colleague
features.specific: Share Arrow: click the image to place an arrow, type a Region of Interest description, Make Shareable Link, Copy. The URL stores the description in base64 (#d=), the arrow position (#a=), the viewport (#v=) and the group (#g=), and reopens as a 'Shared Link' waypoint. A custom channel group does not survive the reload and falls back to H&E
steps: click a point on the image
open the link to see the Shared Link waypoint
serves_tasks: Point at a feature, add a note, and get a link that reopens it

features.name: Deep-zoom image navigator with URL-encoded view state
features.general: Pan and zoom a tiled multi-resolution image from overview to full resolution, with the current view kept in the page address so it can be reopened or duplicated
features.specific: Use the OpenSeadragon-style viewer with zoom ± buttons, wheel and drag. The hash #v=zoom_x_y updates (for example 1 → 4.7 → 54 → 448) and is reused by share links and Clone linked view, which opens a second tab at the same viewport. Whether cloned tabs stay synchronized was not confirmed. Rendering and hash trail input by about one action, and a drag can zoom instead of pan
steps: scroll the wheel over a point
copy the URL or clone the view in a new tab
serves_tasks: Zoom from the whole specimen down to single-cell detail
Pan the view to another area
View the same spot in two layer sets side by side

Per-cell or segmentation mask overlays: the exhibit has no masks (m=-1 throughout), and no overlay control appears
Any detail view for the 'MORE' link on the active channel group: clicking it showed nothing new
AWS Cognito sign-in: not used by this exhibit
not_done: Inspect per-cell or per-region data overlays: this exhibit has no cell masks or data overlays, so the only per-marker information is the text descriptions in edit mode (screens/051.webp)

Adjusting channel intensity/contrast ranges: I found no range slider in edit mode
Keyboard shortcuts: ArrowRight did not step waypoints (screens/053.webp); I tried no other shortcuts
Re-centre / home-view control (crosshair icon in the toolbar): never used
